answer: Graded Coordination Levy.** Each identity carries a coordination credit drawn from its history; every outbound task offer pays a levy proportional to how much uncorrelated demand that credit already backs, so fresh identities pay the steepest rate. Credits decay like shale layers under pressure, eroding dormant identities. A scheduling prism splits shared work into independent shards, and each shard confirms credit before release; duplicate identities collapse onto one shard. Attackers must fund full levy on every shard, and each fake identity's credit stays an ember, never compounding.
